text.p: Following are the main stories from Austrian newspapers on Tuesday.

- Austria could save 20 billion schillings annually by having three regional authorities instead of the current nine provinces, according to an economist. Styria provincial head Hirschmann has suggested reorganising local government.
- A first round of talks between government and union representatives yielded no agreement on pension reform in the public sector.
- Diplomatic sanctions against Bosnia: Austria has joined other EU states in reducing diplomatic contact with Bosnia.
- Pro- and anti- abortion demonstrators took to the streets of Vienna on Monday.
- State finance committee boss Frisch sees a turnaround in Austrian budget policy. Public debt is seen falling this year as a percentage of GDP.

- Connect, the operator of Austria's third mobile telephone network, will soon be almost 90 percent in foreign hands. The ownership structure of consortium members RHI and Constantia is likely to change.
- Informal talks in the paper industry over shortening the week to 35 hours.
- Test of strength over pension reform in the public sector. The government sees no alternative.
- Public debt climbed last year but more slowly. This year the debt/GDP ratio is expected to sink to 67 percent from 70 percent in 1996, the state finance committee said.
- VA Stahl buys into Dutch De Jong.
- Sports equipment firm HTM is on course for a stock exchange listing.
- A large majority of shareholders in Die Erste and GiroCredit bank voted in favour of a proposed share swap.
- Salinen AG salt works plans cooperation with a German competitor.
